describe: a road's asphalt seen straight down, no paint, line or marking of any kind

looks.describe: new asphalt: deep near-black binder, a little darker than charcoal, with a coarse chip seal: tightly packed small dark grey chips about a centimetre across, embedded flat, with a few pale ones among them
the same asphalt a little more used: a shade less black, the same chips, soft faint lighter bands of tone where tyres have polished it, no oil spots, no cracks

trial.describe: fresh asphalt, dark charcoal grey binder with a fine even speckle of small grey and pale stones
worn asphalt, a shade lighter and greyer, stones more exposed, a few tiny dark oil spots and hairline cracks no longer than a hand
